conflict_topics: Who should complete Agent D's analysis section for the client pitch
Whether Agent D should work during bereavement versus go be with family
Backup/contingency plan in case Agent D cannot finish and the deadline
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants speak like coworkers balancing personal bereavement and project risk; language is natural and context-dependent.
Agent A repeatedly urges D to leave the laptop: "Leave your laptop. We'll handle it." This repetition prolongs the dispute.
Resolution was made concrete by specifying a deadline and required notification: "upload your work by 10 p.m... If you can't finish it, you must let us know then."
Two identical acceptances from Agent D appear in Round 11, possibly redundant: "Okay. 10 p.m. is fine. I'll upload it then."
evaluation.final_reason: Agent A concedes to letting Agent D take the laptop and carry out the analysis, while imposing a concrete condition and contingency: "Agent D, you can take the laptop. But I need you to upload your work by 10 p.m. tonight. If you can't finish it, you must let us know then." Agent D explicitly accepts that condition: "Okay. 10 p.m. is fine. I'll upload it then."
position_change_notes: Agent A changed position: initially insisted Agent D leave the laptop and go with family, later conceded: "Okay. You're right... Agent D, you can take the laptop." This concession included a new condition (10 p.m. upload).
Agent D consistently maintained they would finish the work and ultimately accepted the formal condition: "I'll upload it then."
Agents B and C maintained the position that it was better and less risky for Agent D to complete the analysis, and that view influenced A's concession.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A offers condolences and volunteers to cover: "You should go home. Don't worry about the pitch, we'll cover for you." Agent D states need to be with family for the cremation; no incompatible demands expressed yet.

Agent B accepts condolence but refuses extra work: "I can't take on more. I'm already covering... and I'm at my limit." This conflicts with Agent A's volunteer to cover, creating a mild disagreement about who will take on D's work.

Agent A urges D to go and leave work; Agent D refuses and insists on taking laptop to finish: "I can't just leave you with my section half-done... I can finish it from home tonight." Directly incompatible positions emerge.

Agent B tentatively accepts D's plan: "If you're sure you can manage it from home... that would be a big help." Agent D reaffirms: "I'll get it done tonight." No new disagreement stated, but the underlying risk/coverage concern remains.

Agent C expresses concern about pressuring D: "But are you sure you can get it done tonight? That's a lot of pressure on you right now." This renews doubt about the plan's feasibility, keeping disagreement over the best approach active.

Agent D reaffirms desire to finish: "It's better for me to finish it tonight." Agent C presses on contingency: "what's our plan B? If something happens and you can't finish it, we're stuck." The incompatibility (relying on D vs needing backup) remains substantive.

Agent A demands D leave laptop and go: "Leave your laptop. We'll handle it. Go be with your family." Agent D strongly refuses: "No, I can't do that... I'm taking my laptop. It will be done tonight." Clear, strong opposing positions.

Agent A reiterates instruction: "I've made my decision. Leave the laptop." Agent B questions practicality: "How will we figure it out? Agent D is the only one who can do the analysis." Positions remain opposed and active.

Agent A stresses risk and insists their group can look at what's left; Agent B counters that they don't know the analysis and that letting D finish is less risky. Continued entrenched disagreement about who should complete the work.

Agent C and B argue for letting D do the analysis; Agent A concedes: "Okay. You're right. We can't do the analysis. Agent D, you can take the laptop. But I need you to upload your work by 10 p.m. tonight. If you can't finish it, you must let us know then." The major incompatibility is narrowed but the new conditional agreement awaits explicit acceptance by D.
Agent D explicitly accepts the condition: "Okay. 10 p.m. is fine. I'll upload it then." Parties whose demands were in conflict have voiced agreement, resolving the dispute.
Agent A thanks D and reiterates sympathy and release to family: "Okay. Thank you, Agent D. Go, be with your family." No substantive disagreement remains.

substantive_insights: Tension arises from competing obligations: duty to family (time-sensitive funeral/cremation) vs responsibility to meet a fixed, expert-dependent deadline.
Team capability constraints matter: multiple agents state they lack the skills to complete the analysis, which strongly shapes risk assessment and preferred solution.
A conditional concession (permission plus a reporting deadline) resolved the dispute by combining specialist ownership with a contingency plan.
Concerns were practical (deadline risk, contingency) rather than moral or identity-based; the agreement addressed the practical concern explicitly.
